headline: Interpretable gene networks from single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data
label: Interpretable Single Cell Analysis Methods
summary: Stability testing and benchmarking now probe whether gene networks inferred from single-cell and spatial data hold up under scrutiny.
synthesis: The dominant thread is making gene-level network inferences from single-cell and spatial data interpretable through explicit stability assessment, localization, or regulatory prioritization. Starlng assesses the stability of co-expression gene nests from single-cell data and selects robust parameters, while DiCoLo localizes differential coexpression without clustering or integration, using Optimal Transport gene graphs. NicheCorr and smoothclust extend this logic to spatial transcriptomics, targeting niche-dependent co-expression changes and boundary structure on spatial graphs. DisTwiner applies subgroup-aware Elastic Net logistic regression to macrophage scRNA-seq, and Core Coefficient scores transcription-factor dominance in regulatory networks. What is new is the focus on localized, niche-specific, or stability-checked relationships rather than global network summaries. A pan-cancer PANDA/LIONESS benchmark across 9,778 tumors addresses the parallel question of how patient-specific network features are best selected and clustered.
